best_parts: node ladder_hida: mechanism probe (non-filling gallbladder on HIDA versus CT wall signs versus MRCP duct stone), each distractor a different wrong model, retest of TR2 in a new form
node ladder_t_hida_first: names the 'first versus most accurate' confusion, then a sure_note split of the two words
node tg_recog: three TR7 distractors each embody a different wrong rule (imaging in suspected, one local plus imaging, two systemic signs)
flaws: node tg_recog and tg_vig: replay the S3 goal (suspected versus definite rule as a recognition quiz). S4 should apply the rule, not re-teach it. Penalised under R3 depth.
node ladder_case: the key 'Ultrasound of the upper abdomen' is the only option without 'scan', so it is findable by form (DP1).
node tg_recog: 'Two systemic signs, such as fever and high CRP' is weak; a learner who knows a local sign is required discards it (DP2 candidate).
segment-wide: no explain node and no fast lane; every idea is delivered only inside feedback after a miss or hit.

best_parts: node gb_ok: skip lane ('I am sure, skip the lesson') goes to duct_predict and still carries the O4 claim (K3, K49) in the feedback, so no objective is dropped
node gb_explain: a separate explain node (ultrasound as first look, HIDA as the sharper question) after the correct answer, a different second explanation
node ct_predict and ct_t2: the complication question separated from the first-look question, with 'the question changed, so the test should change' as the sure_note
flaws: node gb_predict: key 'HIDA (cholescintigraphy) scan' is the longest option and the only one with a parenthetical, so it is findable by form (DP1).
node tg_predict: key 'Definite, since the imaging findings complete the rule' is the longest option and the only one with an explanatory clause (DP1).
node tg_predict: the only TG18 probe in S4, so TR7 has no second probe in this segment; the re-test is deferred to later segments.
segment-wide: only four probes for three objectives and six traps; retrieval density is thinner than variants a and c.

best_parts: node case_a with case_b and case_c and case_d: interleaved 'two patients, one gallbladder' contrast cases, so the learner discriminates between the investigations rather than recalling one list
node case_a_t_hida and case_a_why: 'Show me why' (deeper) gives a second explanation that contrasts 'first' with 'most accurate' in two sentences
node case_d and case_d_t_need: the TG18 level is applied with imaging as the third set, not replayed as a rule; each distractor maps to a distinct wrong model
flaws: node case_b: key 'No gallbladder filling on HIDA with duodenal tracer' is the longest option (DP1).
node case_d: 'Suspected; needs another local sign' is weak for a learner who already holds that suspected needs A plus B, so it is close to dominated (DP2 candidate).
node case_a: the opening 'Read each stem for its key word' cues the answer frame before the learner commits, which lowers the diagnosticity of the first probe.
segment-wide: no fast lane (no skip) and no hint on case_b or case_c beyond a single hint.

merge_ideas: c's interleaved case probes and 'Show me why' deeper node, plus b's skip lane after a correct probe (routing back to the next case), would add the missing fast lane to c.
a's ladder_hida mechanism probe and sure_note wording, plus c's contrast framing, would give a stronger first-versus-confirm pairing without the S3 replay in a's tg_recog.
Replace a's tg_recog and tg_vig with c's case_d application (imaging as the third set) to stop the S3 replay while keeping a's three distinct TR7 distractors.
